<ul>
<li class="a-spacing-base">
<strong><span class="a-text-bold">Home Theaters: </span></strong>MLV is perfect for creating a cinema-like experience by blocking external noise and preventing sound from escaping, ensuring optimal audio quality inside the room.</li>
<li class="a-spacing-base">
<strong><span class="a-text-bold">Recording Studios: </span></strong>In professional and home recording studios, MLV reduces unwanted noise, echoes, and sound transmission, providing a controlled acoustic environment for clearer recordings.</li>
<li class="a-spacing-base">
<strong><span class="a-text-bold">Apartments and Homes: </span></strong>MLV sheets can be installed on walls, floors, and ceilings to minimize noise transfer between rooms or apartments, offering a quieter living space by reducing loud neighbors, footsteps, or outside traffic sounds.</li>
<li class="a-spacing-base">
<strong><span class="a-text-bold">Office Spaces: </span></strong>It’s ideal for soundproofing conference rooms, private offices, or open-plan spaces, improving privacy and reducing distractions by preventing noise from traveling between rooms.</li>
<li class="a-spacing-base">
<strong><span class="a-text-bold">Machinery and Equipment Enclosures: </span></strong>MLV is often used to wrap around loud machinery or HVAC systems in industrial settings to dampen noise, protecting employees from excessive noise exposure and improving workplace conditions.</li>
<li class="a-spacing-base">
<span class="a-text-bold"><strong>Automotive Soundproofing:</strong> </span>In vehicles, MLV is installed under carpets, in door panels, or in the trunk to reduce road noise, engine sounds, and vibrations, offering a quieter and more comfortable driving experience.</li>
<li class="a-spacing-base">
<span class="a-text-bold"><strong>Hotels and Hospitality:</strong> </span>Hotels use MLV in walls and ceilings to provide guests with a peaceful environment by blocking sounds from adjacent rooms, hallways, or external noise sources.</li>
<li class="a-spacing-base">
<strong><span class="a-text-bold">Hospitals and Medical Facilities: </span></strong>To maintain patient privacy and minimize distractions, MLV can be installed in medical offices, consultation rooms, or waiting areas, ensuring a quiet and confidential environment.</li>
<li class="a-spacing-base">
<span class="a-text-bold"><strong>Commercial Buildings:</strong> </span>From retail stores to restaurants, MLV helps control noise levels, creating a more pleasant atmosphere by blocking noise from other businesses, streets, or equipment.</li>
<li class="a-spacing-base">
<strong><span class="a-text-bold">Doors and Windows: </span></strong>MLV can be applied to doors and windows to prevent sound leakage, providing an effective solution for reducing outdoor noise in urban areas or high-traffic zones.</li>
</ul>

  • CERTIFIED SAFETY STANDARDS: Meets BS EN 1021-1:1994 (Cigarette) and BS 7176:1995 Low Hazard standards, making it a reliable and safe choice for both residential and commercial spaces.
  • EXCELLENT COLOR & WEAR RESISTANCE:  Rated 5+ for lightfastness and high rubbing fastness (wet: 5, dry: 4.5), ensuring colors remain vibrant and the fabric maintains quality over time.
  • VERSATILE APPLICATIONS: Perfect for making acoustic panels, wall coverings, speaker grills, recording studios, home theaters, offices, and architectural interiors.
  • FUNCTIONAL & AESTHETIC: Combines effective soundproofing qualities with a stylish woven jute texture, enhancing both the performance and look of your space.

column2: Timber Acoustics QRD Sound Diffusers
column3:
A Quadratic diffuser comprises wells of different depths, causing a mixture of phase shifts that diffuse reflected sound. They are used to control reflections in the listening environment, particularly from rear walls and first-reflection points. They are based upon prime numbers and each prime number has a different frequency response. Quadratic diffusers can be used alone but the best way to achieve good results is to use multiple panels, side by side. A quadratic diffuser that is placed vertically, will diffuse sound energy back into our rooms in a horizontal, fan-like array and a diffuser place horizontally in our room, will spread sound energy out that enters it in a vertical, fan-like array. With both vertical and horizontal diffusers, one can have a two dimensional diffused sound field.
